instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: An Amazon SNS standard topic delivers order events to a partner's HTTPS endpoint and to an Amazon SQS queue of the company. The partner endpoint is sometimes unavailable for several hours, and the events for the partner are lost. The company must keep each undelivered event for the partner so that it can send the event again later. Which combination of actions meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Attach an Amazon SQS standard queue as the dead-letter queue of the partner's HTTPS subscription, and send the stored events again when the partner is back.

options.label: B
options.text: Change the delivery policy of the HTTPS subscription so that Amazon SNS keeps retrying each failed delivery to the partner endpoint for 24 hours.

options.label: C
options.text: Attach an Amazon SQS queue as the dead-letter queue of the SNS topic itself, so that the queue catches the failed deliveries of every subscription of the topic.

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the HTTPS subscription with an AWS Lambda function that calls the partner endpoint and stores each failed event in Amazon S3.

options.label: E
options.text: Create an Amazon SQS standard queue in the same AWS account and Region as the partner's subscription, with a policy that allows the topic to send.

items.stem: A company must react whenever any Amazon EC2 instance in its AWS account changes to the stopped state. The operations team must receive an email within a few minutes, and an existing AWS Lambda function must create a ticket for each stopped instance. Instances are stopped by users in the console, by scripts and by scheduled jobs. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Lambda function that runs every minute, calls DescribeInstances, compares the states with the last run, and sends the email and the ticket.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an AWS CloudTrail trail that writes to an Amazon S3 bucket, and add an S3 event notification that invokes a function to read each log file.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm on the StatusCheckFailed metric of each instance, and send the alarm notifications to an Amazon SNS topic with an email subscription.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule on the default event bus for EC2 stop events, with the Lambda function and an email-subscribed SNS topic as targets.

items.stem: A company uses an AWS Lambda function to process messages from an Amazon SQS standard queue. The event source mapping uses a batch size of 10, and the queue has a redrive policy with a dead-letter queue. When one message in a batch is malformed, the function returns an error for the whole batch. The other nine messages are processed again and again, and at last all ten messages move to the dead-letter queue. Which solution will retry only the malformed message in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on ReportBatchItemFailures in the event source mapping, and change the function to return the IDs of the messages that failed.

options.label: B
options.text: Lower the visibility timeout of the queue so that a failed batch returns to the function sooner and the good messages finish faster.

options.label: C
options.text: Change the function to delete each message that it processes without error from the queue, and then return an error for the batch when one message fails.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure an on-failure destination for the function that sends the records of failed invocations to a second SQS queue for review.
